question: Can delay, reverb and PCM taps run inside one TuneJS-owned processor node on every host, with the same kernel as the offline renderer, so they no longer depend on host fan-out?

results.pre-existing rows: raw and adapter-scheduled fixtures and live probes v2 unchanged from the 2026-09-12 runs (the 14 native offline failures are the documented fan-out/summation/zero-delay host limits)

conclusions: Delay and reverb are now supported on the native adapter through the TuneJS DSP path when the host app passes react-native-worklets' createSynchronizable and scheduleOnRN; capabilities.delay/reverb/taps/recorder/meters read true there. hostLimits.fanOut stays false: user-level fan-out still rejects.
Native PCM taps have a producer-side engine-frame origin (the worklet callback's currentTime) and the same bounded in-flight/drop accounting as the browser tap. Chunks are always stereo on this host.

Microphone capture on native is still UNSUPPORTED: the RecorderAdapterNode input pool can drop frames without reporting them (docs/backend-decision.md capture findings); a tap after that node would timestamp correctly but could not account for upstream drops.
Live and offline outputs now share one kernel, but sample equality between live host output and Engine.render is still not claimed: sources, gains, filters and pans remain host nodes live.

The intermittent react-native-worklets launch crash is a host issue that predates this wave; it occurred on 1 of 2 Android launches in the final run and never after a relaunch. It is recorded, not fixed.
